summary: Initial migration discovery: Cygnus is evaluating moving inference from OpenAI (and some vLLM on prem experiments) to Redwood Dedicated or Private. Main drivers are cost control, latency predictability, and data residency. Key concerns: model parity vs OpenAI, compatibility with current TGI/vLLM-based tooling, and SOC2/KMS compliance.
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-04 15:00 PT | Duration: 42 min | Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Reilly (CTO, Cygnus), Sara Patel (Head of ML), Noah Kim (Infra Lead)

[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you carving time. I'm Jared from Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. Could you do quick intros?
[00:10] Liam: Yeah sure, Liam O'Reilly, CTO at Cygnus Health. We're building a clinical summarization product, heavy on PHI, so security and residency are big.
[00:18] Sara: Hi I'm Sara, Head of ML, I own model infra and evaluation. We're currently using OpenAI for most generation but we've been experimenting with vLLM and TGI on prem for cost-sensitive workloads.
[00:30] Noah: Noah, infra lead, I manage k8s clusters and networking. We have strict egress policies and are exploring dedicated/private options.
[00:40] Priya: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: understand current stack and pain points, go over Redwood Dedicated/Private differences, compatibility with vLLM/TGI and model parity concerns, then next steps.

[01:05] Sara: I'll be blunt — OpenAI works but it's getting expensive as we scale and latency variability hits SLAs. Our vLLM experiments looked promising on cost but we hit reliability/ops overhead.
[01:20] Jared: Totally, that's a common pattern. For clarity, when you say vLLM/TGI, are you running open weights locally or using a managed vendor?
[01:28] Sara: Mostly local; we run TGI with some quantized models, LoRA adapters. We hit differences in output quality vs OpenAI, some prompt engineering fixed it but it's noisy.
[01:40] Priya: Got it. Two things we normally surface: compatibility & eval parity. Compatibility — our Dedicated runtime supports standard model formats and common tokenizers; we also have guidance for TGI/vLLM workflows. Eval parity — we help run side-by-side evals against OpenAI baselines to quantify delta.

[02:05] Liam: Can you speak to kernels and performance? We care about p99 latency for interactive docs — sub 300ms token ideally.
[02:15] Priya: Sure; Dedicated hosts inference on GPU pools with optimized kernels, dynamic batching, and KV cache management. Realistic p99 depends on model size and sequence lengths; we can run a micro-benchmark with your prompts. Beats noisy self-host patterns because we handle the batching and routing.
[02:35] Noah: Our main constraint is egress and no PHI leaving the VPC. So Private deployment is attractive but we need to understand control plane tradeoffs.
[02:46] Jared: Right — Private (VPC) gives you customer-controlled network and on-prem options, plus KMS integrations. We can share SOC2 and architecture docs — I'll add that to next steps.

[03:05] Sara: How do you handle model upgrades and rollouts? We can't afford regressions in model outputs that affect clinical summaries.
[03:14] Priya: We provide version pinning, canary rollouts, and eval hooks. Our Redwood Console lets you define prompt sets and monitor regression alerts. For clinical use, we'd recommend a canary with a small percentage traffic and evaluation on your golden prompts.

[03:40] Liam: One thing — our team has built tooling around TGI for LoRA injection and custom tokenizers. Will moving to Redwood break that?
[03:48] Priya: Not necessarily. We support custom tokenizers and provide adapter patterns for LoRA/PEFT. There's sometimes friction with export formats; we usually run a conversion step and test on a dev pool. We can pair on that during the pilot.

[04:10] Sara: About eval parity — our baseline is OpenAI gpt-4o-ish endpoints for summarization. We need a metricized comparison: ROUGE, clinical accuracy checks, and a human review sample. How close can Redwood models get?
[04:26] Jared: We recommend a 3-day benchmark: run your prompt set across OpenAI baseline and the candidate dedicated model (or private-hosted copy). We'll capture token-level latency, cost, and quality metrics. In many migrations we've seen parity with carefully-selected open models plus prompt engineering; in some cases customers keep a hybrid — hosted for edge-case quality and Dedicated for bulk.

[05:00] Noah: Network and throughput — can Dedicated autoscale? We have diurnal spikes during business hours.
[05:06] Priya: Yes, Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and surge capacity. You can configure minimum reserved pools for predictable throughput and allow burst to absorb spikes. For Private on-prem, autoscaling depends on your infra but we provide operators and guidance.

[05:30] Liam: Compliance — SOC2, ISO, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS for key management are musts. Can you confirm?
[05:40] Jared: Yep — we have SOC2 Type II (link to docs), SAML SSO, RBAC controls in Console, and KMS/HSM integrations for Private. I'll send the security pack.

[06:05] Sara: Any gotchas with prompt and token accounting? Our billing team wants predictable unit economics.
[06:12] Priya: Redwood provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per-route and per-model in the Console. For Dedicated we give clearer unit costs because you reserve capacity; for Hosted, it's usage-based. We can model your expected monthly run-rate and show TCO.

[06:40] Liam: On the topic of model compatibility — we have LoRA adapters and a custom data pipeline for retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG). Is Redwood compatible with RAG stacks?
[06:50] Priya: Absolutely: we support tool calling, structured outputs, and common RAG patterns. For index and retriever choices, we integrate at the request layer; you can keep your retriever and call our endpoints for generation.

[07:10] Sara: We also use some multi-turn chat state with KV caching — how portable is that?
[07:16] Priya: Our runtime has KV cache management and prefix caching — we expose hooks so your session management can be preserved. There's sometimes small differences in cache semantics vs custom vLLM setups, but we can align in testing.

[07:40] Noah: Latency numbers please — ballpark for LLaMA2-13B quantized vs GPT-like models.
[07:47] Priya: For 13B quantized on Dedicated with optimized kernels you'll see low tens of ms per token on A100/RTX-class GPUs depending on sequence. p99 interactive might be in the 200-400ms token range; exact depends on batch and seq. We'll include concrete benchmark numbers in the follow-up.

[08:20] Liam: How about fallback strategies if capacity is constrained? We can't fail customer requests.
[08:27] Jared: We do smart routing and policy-based fallbacks — route to a cheaper variant or a hosted fallback temporarily. For sensitive PHI workloads you'd probably prefer queuing or reserved capacity rather than fallback, but we can design policies.

[08:50] Sara: Cost delta — rough expectation vs OpenAI?
[08:53] Priya: Migrating to Dedicated often reduces per-token costs 30-70% depending on utilization and model choice. The savings come from reserved capacity and caching/batching efficiencies. We'll run a TCO model for you.

[09:15] Liam: Our ops team uses Terraform and terraform automation — any infra-as-code support?
[09:21] Priya: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we provide Terraform modules and API-driven deployment orchestration. For Private we have an operator package.

[09:40] (brief cross-talk)

[10:05] Sara: What about data retention and audit logs for clinical record drafts? We need immutable audit trails.
[10:12] Jared: You can configure retention policies; we provide audit logs and per-request metadata. For Private deployments you control the storage; Hosted can meet compliance with contractual terms.

[10:40] Noah: One more technical — our current TGI stack uses certain ops knobs (flash attention flags, nvfuser kernels). Does Redwood expose kernel-level tuning?
[10:50] Priya: Not to the kernel-level knobs publicly, but our runtime picks kernels automatically and we can surface perf flags and profiles to you. In enterprise engagements we do tuning with your SEs.

[11:10] Sara: If we do a pilot, what does success look like? We want <10% degradation on clinical accuracy vs OpenAI, 30-50% cost reduction, and p95 latency below 600ms.
[11:20] Jared: That's a good SLO. Proposed pilot: 3 day comparative benchmark + 2 week pilot with live traffic routing for a subset. Deliverables: benchmark report, TCO model, and config for Dedicated/Private.

[11:45] Liam: Timeline — we're aiming to decide in 4 weeks and start a pilot by end of month. Any blockers on your side?
[11:53] Jared: No blockers. We'll send pricing, security docs, and propose benchmark windows.

[12:10] (longer silence then clarifications)

[12:40] Sara: Are there customers who've done similar migrations? Any case studies?
[12:46] Jared: Yes — healthtech and fintech customers. I'll link a couple case studies. Most kept a hybrid during ramp.

[13:05] Noah: Onboarding time for Dedicated vs Private?
[13:10] Priya: Dedicated can be provisioned in a couple weeks with reserved pools; Private depends on infra but pilot packaging is usually 3-6 weeks.

[13:35] Liam: Cost of reserved capacity commitment?
[13:38] Jared: Depends on GPU size and term; we'll include options for monthly and annual commits in the pricing doc.

[14:00] Sara: Any incompatibilities with tokenizers and input preprocessing?
[14:05] Priya: Rarely — we support custom tokenizers but sometimes remapping is needed, we handle it in integration.

[14:30] (discussion about shared artifacts)

[15:00] Priya: I'll summarize next steps: we'll run a short benchmark using your prompt set, share SOC2/security pack, and send Dedicated pricing + SOW.
[15:10] Sara: Sounds good. One ask — please include the exact test harness you use so we can reproduce locally.
[15:16] Priya: Yes, we'll share the harness repo link and instructions.

[15:35] Liam: Thanks, that covers it.

[15:40] Jared: Great — I'll follow up with the docs and proposed benchmark windows. Appreciate the time everyone.

[15:48] Call ended.

Notes: transcription includes some minor mis-heard words (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache in auto-transcript), and occasional speaker label swaps in edges. Shared links mentioned: Redwood Dedicated overview (https://redwood.ai/docs/dedicated), security pack (link to secure docs), benchmark harness repo (internal link).
